directive: 3-5 irregular vertical particle columns with Gaussian X-spread, additive blend, top-opaque bottom-transparent height falloff, warm white-gold on pure black, large 12px soft-circle sprites — volumetric god-rays through fog
anti_patterns_hit: sizeAttenuation-at-distance — formula `12.0 * uPixel * (8.0 / vFogDepth)` at camera-to-particle depth ~28 units renders sprites at ~3–4 px, not the intended 12 px; columns read as microscopic streaks instead of volumetric beams

god-ray planes effectively invisible — plane alpha ceiling is `beam * vert * shimmer * fogF * 0.08`; at 25-unit depth fogF ≈ 0.64, yielding max alpha ~0.051 with AdditiveBlending against black — indistinguishable from background
reasoning: The perspective-scaled point-size formula reproduces the sizeAttenuation-far-camera failure exactly — 12 px becomes ~3 px at the 28-unit camera depth, collapsing the god-ray-column concept into faint hairlines; the supplementary god-ray Mesh planes compound the problem by emitting effectively zero luminance at 0.05 alpha additive.
extractable_ideas: 5-column irregular Gaussian X-spread layout (asymmetric sigma_x per column: 1.4–2.2) — structurally distinct from uniform grids, worth preserving as a particle arrangement primitive
phase-staggered looping descent via `mod(localY + t * speed, colH)` with per-particle random phase — smooth perpetual recycling with no pop artifacts, reusable in any descending-particle piece
height-based alpha gradient (`1 - smoothstep(0.3, 1.0, heightFrac)`) as a directional presence cue — clean and intentional, pairs well with any vertical form
warm white-gold (1.0, 0.96, 0.78) restrained palette on pure black — avoids over-saturated gold while reading as luminous; worth propagating to future warm-light pieces
god-ray planes positioned behind columns as supplementary luminance layer — the architecture is right; fix by raising alpha coefficient to 0.18–0.25 and reducing fog density to 0.008

directive: Transform differential growth tower into turbulent ink-field: each growing vertex emits short ink stroke in local curl direction, birth position maps to hue (acid green/cobalt/magenta gradient), thick overlapping strokes create textile-like pressurized surface
anti_patterns_hit: faint/invisible form — base alpha 0.5 < 0.55 threshold with AdditiveBlending
faint/invisible form — linewidth:2 silently clamps to 1px in WebGL, annihilating the 'thick textile' concept
reasoning: The stroke material uses opacity:0.5 (below the 0.55 floor) combined with AdditiveBlending against a dark background — per bug.md this reliably produces near-invisible marks; compounding the failure, WebGL ignores linewidth>1 on virtually all platforms, so the 'pressurized textile' effect degrades to 1px hairlines that vanish rather than building the thick overlapping surface the directive intended.
extractable_ideas: birth-position → hue mapping (acid green 120° → cobalt → magenta 300°) is a precise, reusable gradient encoding worth keeping
differential-growth vertices as explicit emission sites for curl-traced ink strokes is a strong structural idea — vertex birth drives visual flourish
curl noise used to determine per-stroke travel direction (not just displacement jitter) creates coherent flow fields from chaotic growth
stroke-step integration loop (follow curl vector, unit-normalize per step) is a clean idiom for generating organic path geometry from a field
swap LineBasicMaterial for point-sprite sheets or custom ShaderMaterial with hard alpha (alphaTest≥0.5) to recover the textile density idea without the opacity/linewidth failure modes
